figures.caption: Figure S1: AIMD Snapshots for LiDyS2 and Li6ZnGe2O8. The two materials are at the boundary of the normalized MSD parameter between the passivating and reactive interfaces (see Figure 1 in the main text). After the simulation, LiDySS2 maintains it’s crystal structure while some reactivity is seen at its interface, while the Li6ZnGe2O8 original crystal structure is not present anymore as Li moves into the cell, making it a reactive interface.

figures.caption: Figure S2: Relationship of ∆Eformation and Normalized MSD values. For materials in the training set, their normalized MSD values, calculated as described in the main text, are compared to the driving force for chemical mixing for each Li—SSE pair. Those with bigger driving force tend to show more displacement, though outliers in each group hint at the need to take into account the structure of the SSE when considering the thermodynamic driving force for classifying the reactivity of a particular interface.

figures.label: S7
figures.caption: Figure S7: Training models with different feature sets. Training on linear models using the data split described in the main text for RM and SM are performed with composition (magpie) and structural features from matminer, as well as the features used in the main text. L1 regularization is done for both in this case as opposed to the L2 regularization with combinatorial search used in the main text. The number of features in the matminer set are too large to combinatorially search through at higher N feature models. Instead all features are used in the model, and the regularization strength is changed. At higher inverse regularization more and more features include non-zero coefficients and are effectively N feature models.
